173:       } else if (character === '`') {
174:         result += ' ';
175:         state = 'template';
176:       } else {
177:         result += character;
178:       }
179:       continue;
180:     }
181:     if (state === 'lineComment') {
182:       if (character === '\n') {
183:         result += '\n';
184:         state = 'code';
185:       } else result += ' ';
186:       continue;

188:     if (state === 'blockComment') {
189:       if (character === '*' && next === '/') {
190:         result += '  ';
191:         state = 'code';
192:         index += 1;
193:       } else result += character === '\n' ? '\n' : ' ';
194:       continue;

196:     result += character === '\n' ? '\n' : ' ';

199:     } else if (character === '\\') {

201:     } else if (

204:       (state === 'template' && character === '`')

206:       state = 'code';
207:     }

212: async function materializeModules(
213:   tempRoot: string,
214:   blocks: JsdocExampleBlock[],
215:   imports: Record<string, string>,
216: ): Promise<{ modules: SyntheticExampleModule[]; policyDiagnostics: PrecompileDiagnostic[] }> {
217:   const modules: SyntheticExampleModule[] = [];
218:   const policyDiagnostics: PrecompileDiagnostic[] = [];
219:   for (const [index, block] of blocks.entries()) {
220:     if (!block.compilationExtension) continue;
221:     const forbidden = forbiddenSpecifier(block, imports);
222:     if (forbidden) {
223:       policyDiagnostics.push({
224:         message: `${ownerLabel(block)}: ${forbidden}`,
225:         failureClass: 'badSpecifier',
226:         block,
227:         tsCodes: [],
228:       });
229:       continue;
230:     }
231:     if (block.exemptionReason !== undefined) continue;
232:     const placeholder = invalidPlaceholder(block);
233:     if (placeholder) {
234:       policyDiagnostics.push({
235:         message: `${ownerLabel(block)}: ${placeholder.message}`,
236:         failureClass: 'typeError',
237:         block,
238:         tsCodes: placeholder.tsCodes,
239:       });
240:       continue;
241:     }
242:     const directory = join(tempRoot, 'examples', String(index + 1));
243:     const preamblePath = join(directory, 'preamble.ts');
244:     const modulePath = join(directory, `example.${block.compilationExtension}`);
245:     await writeSnippetFile(preamblePath, preamble());
246:     const symbolImport = exampleSymbolImport(block);
247:     const header = [`// ${ownerLabel(block)}`, `import './preamble.ts';`];
248:     if (symbolImport) header.push(symbolImport);
249:     await writeSnippetFile(modulePath, `${header.join('\n')}\n${block.body}\n`);
250:     modules.push({ block, path: modulePath, headerLines: header.length });
251:   }
252:   return { modules, policyDiagnostics };
253: }

255: function escapeRegExp(value: string): string {
256:   return value.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
257: }
258: 
259: function mapDiagnostics(raw: string, modules: SyntheticExampleModule[]): string {
260:   let mapped = raw;
261:   for (const module of modules) {
262:     const label = ownerLabel(module.block);
263:     for (const generated of [module.path, toFileUrl(module.path).href]) {
264:       mapped = mapped.replace(
265:         new RegExp(`${escapeRegExp(generated)}:(\\d+):(\\d+)`, 'g'),
266:         (_match, line: string, column: string) =>
267:           `${label}:${Math.max(1, Number(line) - module.headerLines)}:${column}`,
268:       );
269:       mapped = mapped.replaceAll(generated, label);
270:     }
271:   }
272:   return mapped;
273: }
274: 
275: function classifyDiagnostics(
276:   raw: string,
277:   modules: SyntheticExampleModule[],
278:   policyDiagnostics: PrecompileDiagnostic[],
279:   analysis: JsdocExampleAnalysis,
280: ): {
281:   failureCensus: JsdocFailureCensus;
282:   typeErrorExamples: JsdocTypeErrorExample[];
283:   classifiedCompilerFailureCount: number;
284: } {
285:   const census = emptyFailureCensus(analysis);
286:   const precompiledTypeErrors = policyDiagnostics
287:     .filter((finding) => finding.failureClass === 'typeError')
288:     .map((finding): JsdocTypeErrorExample => ({
289:       failureClass: 'typeError',
290:       owner: finding.block.owner,
291:       exampleOrdinal: finding.block.exampleOrdinal,
292:       fenceOrdinal: finding.block.fenceOrdinal,
293:       tsCodes: finding.tsCodes,
294:     }));
295:   census.badSpecifier =
296:     policyDiagnostics.filter((finding) => finding.failureClass === 'badSpecifier').length;
297:   census.typeError = precompiledTypeErrors.length;
298:   const compiler = classifyDenoCheckDiagnostics(raw, modules);
299:   census.badSpecifier += compiler.census.badSpecifier;
300:   census.typeError += compiler.census.typeError;
301:   census.unboundName += compiler.census.unboundName;
302:   return {
303:     failureCensus: census,
304:     typeErrorExamples: [...precompiledTypeErrors, ...compiler.typeErrorExamples],
305:     classifiedCompilerFailureCount: Object.values(compiler.census).reduce(
306:       (sum, count) => sum + count,
307:       0,
308:     ),
309:   };
310: }
311: 
312: /**
313:  * Count compiler diagnostics that no example module owns.
314:  *
315:  * `classifyDenoCheckDiagnostics` attributes a diagnostic by matching its `at <path>` against a
316:  * synthetic module. Anything it cannot match — a support file, or the preamble — was previously
317:  * invisible: `unclassifiedCompilerFailure` only fired when *zero* diagnostics were classified, which
318:  * is never true while the deferred corpus is non-empty. A whole class of error could therefore
319:  * vanish. These are counted and reported so the gate fails instead.
320:  */
321: export function unattributedDiagnostics(
322:   raw: string,
323:   modules: ReadonlyArray<{ path: string }>,
324: ): string[] {
325:   const normalized = stripAnsi(raw);
326:   const owned = modules.flatMap((module) => [module.path, toFileUrl(module.path).href]);
327:   const unattributed: string[] = [];
328:   for (
329:     const match of normalized.matchAll(/TS(\d+) \[ERROR\]:[\s\S]*?\n\s+at ([^\n]+):(\d+):(\d+)/g)
330:   ) {
331:     const location = match[2] ?? '';
332:     if (owned.some((path) => location.startsWith(path))) continue;
333:     unattributed.push(`TS${match[1]} at ${location}:${match[3]}:${match[4]}`);
334:   }
335:   return unattributed;
336: }
337: 
338: /**
339:  * Classify each synthetic module from deterministic, ANSI-independent Deno diagnostics.
340:  *
341:  * All classes are enforced failures. Published-API type errors also retain their owner and
342:  * diagnostic codes for the attributable census.
343:  */
344: export function classifyDenoCheckDiagnostics(
345:   raw: string,
346:   modules: ReadonlyArray<{ path: string; block: JsdocExampleBlock }>,
347: ): DiagnosticClassification {
348:   const census = { badSpecifier: 0, typeError: 0, unboundName: 0 };
349:   const typeErrorExamples: JsdocTypeErrorExample[] = [];
350:   const normalized = stripAnsi(raw);
351:   for (const module of modules) {
352:     const paths = [module.path, toFileUrl(module.path).href];
353:     const relatedCodes = [
354:       ...normalized.matchAll(/TS(\d+) \[ERROR\]:[\s\S]*?\n\s+at ([^\n]+):(\d+):(\d+)/g),
355:     ]
356:       .filter((match) => paths.some((path) => match[2]?.startsWith(path)))
357:       .map((match) => Number(match[1]));
358:     if (relatedCodes.length === 0) continue;
359:     const tsCodes = [...new Set(relatedCodes)].sort((a, b) => a - b);
360:     if (relatedCodes.some((code) => code === 2305 || code === 2307 || code === 2724)) {
361:       census.badSpecifier += 1;
362:     } else if (relatedCodes.some((code) => code === 2304 || code === 2552 || code === 18004)) {
363:       census.unboundName += 1;
364:     } else {
365:       census.typeError += 1;
366:       typeErrorExamples.push({
367:         failureClass: 'typeError',
368:         owner: module.block.owner,
369:         exampleOrdinal: module.block.exampleOrdinal,
370:         fenceOrdinal: module.block.fenceOrdinal,
371:         tsCodes,
372:       });
373:     }
374:   }
375:   return { census, typeErrorExamples };
376: }
377: 
378: /** Compile published JSDoc examples in isolated modules without importing or executing them. */
379: export async function compileJsdocExamples(
380:   analysis: JsdocExampleAnalysis,
381:   repositoryRoot: string,
382: ): Promise<JsdocExampleCompilationResult> {
383:   const failureCensus = emptyFailureCensus(analysis);
384:   const policyErrors = analysis.findings.filter((finding) =>
385:     finding.disposition === 'unfenced' || finding.disposition === 'malformed'
386:   );
387:   if (analysis.census.candidates === 0 || analysis.census.checked === 0) {
388:     const condition = analysis.census.candidates === 0 ? 'zero candidates' : 'zero checked modules';
389:     return {
390:       code: 1,
391:       diagnostics: `empty selection refused: ${condition}; deno check was not spawned`,
392:       failureCensus,
393:       enforcedFailureCount: enforcedFailures(failureCensus),
394:       typeErrorExamples: [],
395:       rootLockUnchanged: true,
396:       temporaryLockRewritten: false,
397:       denoCheckSpawned: false,
398:     };
399:   }
400: 
401:   const tempRoot = await Deno.makeTempDir({ prefix: 'netscript-jsdoc-examples-' });
402:   const rootLockPath = join(repositoryRoot, 'deno.lock');
403:   const rootLockBefore = await Deno.readTextFile(rootLockPath);
404:   try {
405:     const supportImports = await materializeSharedSupports(tempRoot);
406:     const workspace = await resolveWorkspaceSurface(repositoryRoot, supportImports, {
407:       publishedOnly: true,
408:     });
409:     const { modules, policyDiagnostics } = await materializeModules(
410:       tempRoot,
411:       analysis.blocks,
412:       workspace.imports,
413:     );
414:     if (modules.length === 0) {
415:       const classified = classifyDiagnostics('', modules, policyDiagnostics, analysis);
416:       return {
417:         code: 1,
418:         diagnostics: [
419:           ...policyDiagnostics.map((finding) => finding.message),
420:           'empty selection refused: zero checked modules; deno check was not spawned',
421:         ].join('\n'),
422:         failureCensus: classified.failureCensus,
423:         enforcedFailureCount: enforcedFailures(classified.failureCensus),
424:         typeErrorExamples: classified.typeErrorExamples,
425:         rootLockUnchanged: true,
426:         temporaryLockRewritten: false,
427:         denoCheckSpawned: false,
428:       };
429:     }
430:     const configPath = join(tempRoot, 'deno.json');
431:     await Deno.writeTextFile(
432:       configPath,
433:       `${
434:         JSON.stringify(
435:           {
436:             compilerOptions: {
437:               strict: true,
438:               noImplicitAny: true,
439:               noImplicitReturns: true,
440:               isolatedDeclarations: false,
441:               jsx: 'precompile',
442:               jsxImportSource: 'preact',
443:             },
444:             imports: workspace.imports,
445:             catalog: workspace.catalog,
446:           },
447:           null,
448:           2,
449:         )
450:       }\n`,
451:     );
452:     const tempLockPath = join(tempRoot, 'deno.lock');
453:     await Deno.copyFile(rootLockPath, tempLockPath);
454:     // Keep the Windows command line bounded while checking every isolated example module.
455:     const entryPath = join(tempRoot, 'examples.ts');
456:     await Deno.writeTextFile(
457:       entryPath,
458:       `${
459:         modules.map((module) => `import ${JSON.stringify(toFileUrl(module.path).href)};`).join('\n')
460:       }\n`,
461:     );
462:     const output = await new Deno.Command(Deno.execPath(), {
463:       cwd: repositoryRoot,
464:       env: { FORCE_COLOR: '0', NO_COLOR: '1' },
465:       args: [
466:         'check',
467:         '--unstable-kv',
468:         '--lock',
469:         tempLockPath,
470:         '--config',
471:         configPath,
472:         entryPath,
473:       ],
474:       stdout: 'piped',
475:       stderr: 'piped',
476:     }).output();
477:     const stderr = stripAnsi(new TextDecoder().decode(output.stderr));
478:     const rootLockAfter = await Deno.readTextFile(rootLockPath);
479:     const tempLockAfter = await Deno.readTextFile(tempLockPath);
480:     const rootLockUnchanged = rootLockBefore === rootLockAfter;
481:     if (!rootLockUnchanged) throw new Error('tracked root deno.lock changed during JSDoc check');
482:     const classified = classifyDiagnostics(
483:       stderr,
484:       modules,
485:       policyDiagnostics,
486:       analysis,
487:     );
488:     // A diagnostic no example owns must never be silently dropped, even when siblings classified.
489:     const unowned = unattributedDiagnostics(stderr, modules);
490:     const diagnostics = [
491:       ...policyErrors.map((finding) =>
492:         `${finding.owner.sourcePath} · ${finding.owner.kind}${
493:           finding.owner.symbol ? ` ${finding.owner.symbol}` : ''
494:         } · example ${finding.exampleOrdinal}: ${finding.reason}`
495:       ),
496:       ...policyDiagnostics.map((finding) => finding.message),
497:       mapDiagnostics(stderr, modules).trim(),
498:       unowned.length === 0 ? '' : [
499:         `unattributed compiler diagnostics: ${unowned.length}`,
500:         ...unowned.map((entry) => `  ${entry}`),
501:       ].join('\n'),
502:     ].filter(Boolean).join('\n');
503:     const enforcedFailureCount = enforcedFailures(classified.failureCensus);
504:     const unclassifiedCompilerFailure = output.code !== 0 &&
505:       classified.classifiedCompilerFailureCount === 0;
506:     const code = enforcedFailureCount === 0 && !unclassifiedCompilerFailure && unowned.length === 0
507:       ? 0
508:       : 1;
509:     return {
510:       code,
511:       diagnostics,
512:       failureCensus: classified.failureCensus,
513:       enforcedFailureCount,
514:       typeErrorExamples: classified.typeErrorExamples,
515:       rootLockUnchanged,
516:       temporaryLockRewritten: rootLockBefore !== tempLockAfter,
517:       denoCheckSpawned: true,
518:     };
519:   } finally {
520:     await Deno.remove(tempRoot, { recursive: true });
521:   }
522: }

173:   if (kind === 'typeAlias' || kind === 'interface') return 'type';
174:   if (kind === 'class') return 'class';
175:   return 'value';
176: }
177: 
178: function sourcePath(repositoryRoot: string, filename: string): string {
179:   const path = filename.startsWith('file:') ? fromFileUrl(filename) : filename;
180:   return normalize(relative(repositoryRoot, path)).replaceAll('\\', '/');
181: }
182: 
183: function symbolExamples(
184:   repositoryRoot: string,
185:   entry: ExportEntry,
186:   doc: unknown,
187: ): SymbolExample[] {
188:   const module = docModule(doc, entry.path);
189:   if (!module) return [];
190:   const result: SymbolExample[] = [];
191:   for (const symbol of objects(module.symbols)) {
192:     if (typeof symbol.name !== 'string') continue;
193:     for (const declaration of objects(symbol.declarations)) {
194:       const docs = isObject(declaration.jsDoc) ? declaration.jsDoc : undefined;
195:       const docsTags = docs ? tags(docs) : [];
196:       if (exampleDocs(docs).length === 0) continue;
197:       const location = isObject(declaration.location) ? declaration.location : undefined;
198:       if (!location || typeof location.filename !== 'string') continue;
199:       const path = sourcePath(repositoryRoot, location.filename);
200:       const kind = declarationKind(declaration.kind);
201:       result.push({
202:         owner: {
203:           memberName: entry.memberName,
204:           memberRoot: entry.memberRoot,
205:           sourcePath: path,
206:           kind: 'symbol',
207:           symbol: symbol.name,
208:           publicSpecifier: entry.specifier,
209:           declarationKind: kind,
210:         },
211:         declarationPath: path,
212:         declarationLine: typeof location.line === 'number' ? location.line : 1,
213:         tags: docsTags,
214:       });
215:     }
216:   }
217:   return result;
218: }
219: 
220: function bindingPreference(a: SymbolExample, b: SymbolExample): number {
221:   const aSpecifier = a.owner.publicSpecifier ?? '';
222:   const bSpecifier = b.owner.publicSpecifier ?? '';
223:   return aSpecifier.length - bSpecifier.length || aSpecifier.localeCompare(bSpecifier);
224: }
225: 
226: function dedupeSymbols(examples: SymbolExample[]): SymbolExample[] {
227:   const selected = new Map<string, SymbolExample>();
228:   for (const example of examples.sort(bindingPreference)) {
229:     const key = `${example.declarationPath}:${example.declarationLine}:${example.owner.symbol}`;
230:     if (!selected.has(key)) selected.set(key, example);
231:   }
232:   return [...selected.values()].sort((a, b) =>
233:     a.declarationPath.localeCompare(b.declarationPath) ||
234:     a.declarationLine - b.declarationLine ||
235:     (a.owner.symbol ?? '').localeCompare(b.owner.symbol ?? '')
236:   );
237: }
238: 
239: function analyzeTag(
240:   doc: string,
241:   owner: JsdocExampleOwner,
242:   exampleOrdinal: number,
243:   blocks: JsdocExampleBlock[],
244:   findings: JsdocExampleFinding[],
245: ): void {
246:   const label = `${owner.sourcePath} · ${owner.kind}${
247:     owner.symbol ? ` ${owner.symbol}` : ''
248:   } · example ${exampleOrdinal}`;
249:   let fences;
250:   try {
251:     fences = extractFencedBlocks(doc, label);
252:   } catch (error) {
253:     findings.push({
254:       disposition: 'malformed',
255:       owner,
256:       exampleOrdinal,
257:       reason: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
258:     });
259:     return;
260:   }
261:   if (fences.length === 0) {
262:     findings.push({
263:       disposition: 'unfenced',
264:       owner,
265:       exampleOrdinal,
266:       reason: 'example has no fence',
267:     });
268:     return;
269:   }
270:   for (const fence of fences) {
271:     if (fence.infoString.length === 0) {
272:       findings.push({
273:         disposition: 'malformed',
274:         owner,
275:         exampleOrdinal,
276:         fenceOrdinal: fence.fenceOrdinal,
277:         reason: 'fence has no language',
278:       });
279:       continue;
280:     }
281:     if (!fence.checkedLanguage) {
282:       findings.push({
283:         disposition: 'nonTypeScript',
284:         owner,
285:         exampleOrdinal,
286:         fenceOrdinal: fence.fenceOrdinal,
287:         reason: fence.language,
288:       });
289:       continue;
290:     }
291:     const block: JsdocExampleBlock = {
292:       owner,
293:       exampleOrdinal,
294:       fenceOrdinal: fence.fenceOrdinal,
295:       openingLine: fence.openingLine,
296:       codeStartLine: fence.codeStartLine,
297:       language: fence.language,
298:       checkedLanguage: fence.checkedLanguage,
299:       compilationExtension: fence.compilationExtension,
300:       exemptionReason: fence.exemptionReason,
301:       body: fence.body,
302:     };
303:     blocks.push(block);
304:     findings.push({
305:       disposition: fence.exemptionReason ? 'exempt' : 'checked',
306:       owner,
307:       exampleOrdinal,
308:       fenceOrdinal: fence.fenceOrdinal,
309:       reason: fence.exemptionReason,
310:     });
311:   }
312: }
313: 
314: /** Classify one structured JSDoc example tag with the repository's fence policy. */
315: export function classifyJsdocExampleTag(
316:   doc: string,
317:   owner: JsdocExampleOwner,
318:   exampleOrdinal: number,
319: ): Pick<JsdocExampleAnalysis, 'blocks' | 'findings'> {
320:   const blocks: JsdocExampleBlock[] = [];
321:   const findings: JsdocExampleFinding[] = [];
322:   analyzeTag(doc, owner, exampleOrdinal, blocks, findings);
323:   return { blocks, findings };
324: }
325: 
326: function moduleExampleOwner(file: PublishedSourceFile, repositoryRoot: string): JsdocExampleOwner {
327:   return {
328:     memberName: file.member.name,
329:     memberRoot: file.member.root,
330:     sourcePath: normalize(relative(repositoryRoot, file.path)).replaceAll('\\', '/'),
331:     kind: 'module',
332:   };
333: }
334: 
335: /** Discover and classify the published JSDoc example corpus from Deno's JSON documentation. */
336: export async function analyzeJsdocExamples(
337:   repositoryRoot: string,
338:   options: { loadDoc?: DenoDocLoader } = {},
339: ): Promise<JsdocExampleAnalysis> {
340:   const loadDoc = options.loadDoc ?? loadDenoDocJson;
341:   const files = await discoverPublishedSourceFiles(repositoryRoot);
342:   const entries = await exportedEntrypoints(repositoryRoot, files);
343:   const cache = new Map<string, Promise<unknown>>();
344:   const getDoc = (path: string): Promise<unknown> => {
345:     const canonical = isAbsolute(path) ? path : join(repositoryRoot, path);
346:     const existing = cache.get(canonical);
347:     if (existing) return existing;
348:     const loaded = loadDoc(canonical);
349:     cache.set(canonical, loaded);
350:     return loaded;
351:   };
352:   await loadConcurrently(
353:     [...new Set([...files.map((file) => file.path), ...entries.map((entry) => entry.path)])],
354:     8,
355:     getDoc,
356:   );
357: 
358:   const blocks: JsdocExampleBlock[] = [];
359:   const findings: JsdocExampleFinding[] = [];
360:   const publishedPaths = new Set(
361:     files.map((file) => normalize(relative(repositoryRoot, file.path)).replaceAll('\\', '/')),
362:   );
363:   for (const file of files) {
364:     const module = docModule(await getDoc(file.path), file.path);
365:     const owner = moduleExampleOwner(file, repositoryRoot);
366:     for (const [index, doc] of exampleDocs(module?.module_doc).entries()) {
367:       analyzeTag(doc, owner, index + 1, blocks, findings);
368:     }
369:   }
370: 
371:   const publicSymbols: SymbolExample[] = [];
372:   for (const entry of entries) {
373:     publicSymbols.push(
374:       ...symbolExamples(repositoryRoot, entry, await getDoc(entry.path)).filter((example) =>
375:         publishedPaths.has(example.declarationPath)
376:       ),
377:     );
378:   }
379:   for (const symbol of dedupeSymbols(publicSymbols)) {
380:     for (const [index, doc] of exampleDocs({ tags: symbol.tags }).entries()) {
381:       analyzeTag(doc, symbol.owner, index + 1, blocks, findings);
382:     }
383:   }
384: 
385:   const exemptions = blocks.filter((block) => block.exemptionReason !== undefined);
386:   const members = new Set(files.map((file) => file.member.name)).size;
387:   const census: JsdocExampleCensus = {
388:     members,
389:     files: files.length,
390:     examples: new Set(
391:       findings.map((finding) =>
392:         `${finding.owner.sourcePath}:${finding.owner.kind}:${
393:           finding.owner.symbol ?? ''
394:         }:${finding.exampleOrdinal}`
395:       ),
396:     ).size,
397:     candidates: blocks.length,
398:     checked: blocks.length - exemptions.length,
399:     exempt: exemptions.length,
400:     nonTypeScript: findings.filter((finding) => finding.disposition === 'nonTypeScript').length,
401:     unfenced: findings.filter((finding) => finding.disposition === 'unfenced').length,
402:     malformed: findings.filter((finding) => finding.disposition === 'malformed').length,
403:     failures: 0,
404:   };
405:   return { blocks, findings, exemptions, census };
406: }
407: 
408: /** Public declaration bindings selected by the same exact-owner policy as the corpus. */
409: export function publicSymbolBindings(analysis: JsdocExampleAnalysis): PublicSymbolBinding[] {
410:   return analysis.blocks.flatMap((block) => {
411:     const owner = block.owner;
412:     if (
413:       owner.kind !== 'symbol' || !owner.symbol || !owner.publicSpecifier || !owner.declarationKind
414:     ) return [];
415:     return [{
416:       symbol: owner.symbol,
417:       declarationPath: owner.sourcePath,
418:       declarationKind: owner.declarationKind,
419:       publicSpecifier: owner.publicSpecifier,
420:     }];
421:   });
422: }
423: 
424: /** Render the stable census line consumed by local and durable gate evidence. */
425: export function formatJsdocExampleCensus(
426:   census: JsdocExampleCensus,
427:   status: 'PASS' | 'FAIL',
428: ): string {
429:   return `jsdoc examples: ${status} members=${census.members} files=${census.files} examples=${census.examples} candidates=${census.candidates} checked=${census.checked} exempt=${census.exempt} non_ts=${census.nonTypeScript} unfenced=${census.unfenced} malformed=${census.malformed} failures=${census.failures}`;
430: }
431:

18: # NetScript Harness (V3) — Orchestration Skill
19: 
20: This skill coordinates harness-mode runs. The authoritative harness docs live under `.llm/harness/`;
21: this skill tells you what to load and in what order.
22: 
23: Agent lanes and their model bindings are configuration, not dogma — the single source of truth is
24: [`workflow/lane-policy.md`](../../../.llm/harness/workflow/lane-policy.md). Four rules are hard:
25: **generator-session ≠ evaluator-session**, **generator vendor family ≠ evaluator vendor family**,
26: the **slice review gate** (no implementation lane self-certifies), and **complex/architecture tier
27: selection requires explicit owner or milestone-coordinator authority with a recorded rationale**.
28: Workload tier, role, route, and fallbacks are recorded in the run dir's `supervisor.md`/`drift.md`.
29: 
30: ## When to Use
31: 
32: - The user says `use harness` or asks for a harnessed run.
33: - Selecting archetypes, scope overlays, or gate sets.
34: - Tracking run artifacts, commits, or drift.
35: - Understanding evaluator protocol (PLAN-EVAL or IMPL-EVAL).
36: - Deciding where a lesson or doctrine update should live.
37: 
38: ## When Not to Use
39: 
40: - For package/plugin architecture decisions — use `netscript-doctrine`.
41: - For JSR readiness audits — use `jsr-audit`.
42: - For frontend/framework-specific questions — use `deno-fresh` or the relevant domain skill.
43: 
44: ## Key Concepts
45: 
46: | Concept                 | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                        |
47: | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
48: | **9-phase model**       | Bootstrap → Research → Plan & Design → Plan-Gate → Implement → Gate → Evaluate → Release → Close.                                                                              |
49: | **PLAN-EVAL**           | Conditional pre-implementation pass for complex/decision-heavy work; hard stop when selected.                                                                                  |
50: | **IMPL-EVAL**           | Mandatory final pass after implementation unless the owner explicitly waives it.                                                                                               |
51: | **Routing matrix**      | Five workload tiers and four coordinator tiers with role-specific routes; single source `workflow/lane-policy.md`.                                                             |
52: | **Privileged tiers**    | `complex` and `architecture` fail closed unless the owner or milestone coordinator explicitly authorizes the row and records why.                                              |
53: | **Slice review gate**   | Tier-A supervisor substantively reviews each landed slice before the sign-off commit; no lane self-certifies (A1).                                                             |
54: | **Supervisor identity** | Every run dir carries `supervisor.md` (model, session, host, paths, branch, baseline, lanes).                                                                                  |
55: | **Plan-Gate**           | Checklist (`gates/plan-gate.md`) that PLAN-EVAL enforces.                                                                                                                      |
56: | **Archetype**           | Package/plugin shape profile from `archetypes/ARCHETYPE-*.md`.                                                                                                                 |
57: | **Scope overlay**       | `SCOPE-frontend.md`, `SCOPE-service.md`, `SCOPE-docs.md`.                                                                                                                      |
58: | **Seed run**            | Planning-only run shape (`workflow/seed-run.md`): discovery → roadmap → owner-ratified one-shot GitHub filing. Use when the deliverable is a board (epics + issues), not code. |
59: | **Milestone cluster**   | Release run shape (`workflow/milestone-run.md`): Step 0 intake/cleanup/DAG → four topic orchestrators → direct-to-main leaves → canaries/stable cut.                           |
60: | **Run artifact**        | File in `.llm/runs/<run-id>/` that preserves state across sessions.                                                                                                            |
61: | **Debt**                | Recorded in `.llm/harness/debt/arch-debt.md`.                                                                                                                                  |
62: 
63: For a **supervisor run** (two or more capability-scoped phase groups), also read
64: `.llm/harness/workflow/supervisor.md` and `.llm/harness/workflow/escalation.md`, and track the
65: groups in `phase-registry.md`.
66: 
67: For a **release milestone**, use the milestone-cluster route instead: read
68: `workflow/milestone-run.md` and `agent-milestone-orchestrator`. Do not apply the generic supervisor
69: integration branch. Create the intake, inventory, DAG, cluster-state, and generated status
70: artifacts; Step 0 must validate before any implementation or evaluation lane starts.
71: 
72: For OpenHands or local-agent handoffs during a run, also read
73: `.llm/harness/workflow/agent-handoff.md` and `.agents/skills/openhands-handoff/SKILL.md`.
74: 
75: ## Workflow
76: 
77: The user may still write `profile: package`, `profile: docs`, or similar. In V3 that field is an
78: intent hint, not the final profile.
79: 
80: | User hint                  | V3 selection                                                |
81: | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
82: | `package`                  | identify `ARCHETYPE-1` through `ARCHETYPE-6`                |
83: | `plugin`                   | normally `ARCHETYPE-5`, unless sibling packages also change |
84: | `frontend`                 | affected archetype(s) plus `SCOPE-frontend.md`              |
85: | `service`                  | affected archetype(s) plus `SCOPE-service.md`               |
86: | `docs` or `knowledge-base` | `SCOPE-docs.md` plus any described archetypes               |
87: 
88: 1. Read `workflow/activation.md` and `workflow/run-loop.md`.
89: 2. If resuming, read `.llm/runs/<run-id>/context-pack.md`.
90: 3. Identify the target surface and select archetype + overlays.
91: 4. Read `gates/archetype-gate-matrix.md` and `gates/plan-gate.md`.
92: 5. Scaffold run artifacts from `templates/`.
93: 6. Produce `research.md`, then `plan.md` with locked decisions.
94: 7. Record Design checkpoint in `worklog.md`.
95: 8. **For complex/decision-heavy work, run PLAN-EVAL in a separate session before implementation;
96:    otherwise record a justified `PLAN-EVAL: N/A`.**
97: 9. Implement one commit slice at a time; push + comment on the draft PR (the commit trail) and keep
98:    `worklog.md`/`context-pack.md` current after each.
99: 10. Run gates; record results in `worklog.md`.
100: 11. **Run IMPL-EVAL (separate session) unless the owner explicitly waives it.**
101: 12. Close: update `context-pack.md`, `arch-debt.md`, and promote lessons if warranted.
102: 
103: When the opening diff is docs-only, proactively apply `ci:skip-e2e` to the draft PR and also apply
104: `ci:skip-scaffold` when scaffold-static is not applicable. Use `ci:full` as the escape hatch when
105: the docs-only change must exercise the full CI surface. Record the selection in the opening phase
106: comment so the evaluator can verify that the cheap lane is intentional.
107: 
108: ## Human Review Surface
109: 
110: Keep user-facing plans, issues, PRs, benchmark reports, and handoffs compact. Lead with the
111: decision, measured evidence, total footprint, risk, and next action. Link raw evidence instead of
112: copying run machinery or phase ledgers into the review surface. If the original goal is not obvious
113: on one screen, consolidate and simplify before asking for coordination or review.
114: 
115: ## Agent Delegation Contract
116: 
117: Lane assignments and model bindings are configuration. Operational execution tiers still describe
118: how work is launched, while workload tiers and role bindings are defined once in
119: [`workflow/lane-policy.md`](../../../.llm/harness/workflow/lane-policy.md). Do not restate lane
120: routing here — defer to that file. The items below are the parts of the contract that hold as
121: **invariants** regardless of which lane implements:
122: 
123: - **Generator ≠ evaluator (hard invariant).** The session that generates a plan or an implementation
124:   is never the session that evaluates it. Which model implements is configurable per run and
125:   recorded in `supervisor.md`/`drift.md`; the session separation is not.
126: - **Slice review gate (A1, hard invariant).** After any implementation lane lands a slice and its
127:   automated gates pass, the Tier-A supervisor substantively reviews the slice content before the
128:   sign-off commit — and the sign-off commit is the supervisor's, not the implementer's. This holds
129:   for every implementation tier (B Opus sub-agents, C Workflow-generated slices, D WSL Codex); no
130:   lane self-certifies. See `workflow/lane-policy.md` for the rule and `workflow/run-loop.md` for the
131:   step placement.
132: - **Evaluator route binding.** Select the evaluator from the workload tier and phase in
133:   `workflow/lane-policy.md`, skip candidates from the selected generator's vendor family, and record
134:   the complete route in the run. PLAN-EVAL is risk-selected. Re-steer the same evaluator and obey
135:   the tier-specific round/notification policy; do not substitute a global retry rule.
136: - **Privileged-row authority.** `complex` and `architecture` require explicit owner or
137:   milestone-coordinator authorization plus a recorded rationale. Never promote a task into either
138:   row from complexity inference, file count, or evaluator role alone; cap it at `feature` otherwise.
139: - **Tier-D mobile-visibility proof.** A Tier-D (WSL Codex) implementation slice is launched only via
140:   skills + `.llm/tools/agentic/` (never ad-hoc `wsl.exe`), and only when the run artifacts include
141:   the WSL worktree path, concrete Codex thread id, daemon-managed `remote-control` proof, and the
142:   follow-up steering command for that same thread. Without those, record the launch as
143:   failed/not-attached. Claude helpers (`codex:rescue`, `codex:codex-rescue`, `codex-companion.mjs`,
144:   internal `general-purpose` agents) are local tool surfaces, not daemon-attached Codex threads.
145: - **Per-slice trackability.** Every implementation slice is independently trackable: branch/worktree
146:   identity, agent/thread identity, files touched, tests run, commit hash, push status, and PR
147:   comment/status. Each slice commits, pushes, and comments on the draft PR before the next slice is
148:   considered complete (the draft-PR commit list + per-slice PR comments are the commit trail).
149: - **Green-gate merge bar.** Merge, publish, or release gates require all relevant tests green with
150:   required features intact. For catalog-related work, do not delete, skip, de-catalog, or bypass
151:   tests unless the evaluator verdict explicitly classifies the test as stale/irrelevant and the PR
152:   comment records the rationale.
153: - **Blocked-lane handling.** If an evaluator or implementation launch path is blocked, record the
154:   missing launch mechanism in `worklog.md`/`drift.md`, then proceed only with an owner-authorized
155:   fallback lane recorded in `supervisor.md`/`drift.md`.
156: 
157: ## Common Pitfalls
158: 
159: - **Skipping a selected Plan-Gate** — for complex/decision-heavy work, implementation before
160:   PLAN-EVAL `PASS` is a process failure. Small/mechanical work records `PLAN-EVAL: N/A` first.
161: - **Self-evaluation** — The evaluator must be a separate session. The generator does not
162:   self-certify.
163: - **Wrong evaluator route** — select from the workload tier and phase, preserve separate sessions,
164:   and skip same-vendor-family candidates. Apply the provider order Claude → Codex → Google →
165:   OpenCode Go → Ollama → OpenRouter only among capabilities for the selected logical model. Paid
166:   routes require a fresh expense decision. Record every fallback and requested/observed identity.
167: - **Self-certifying a slice** — a green automated gate is not a sign-off. The Tier-A supervisor must
168:   substantively review the slice before the sign-off commit, for every implementation lane
169:   (`workflow/lane-policy.md` invariant 2). No lane self-certifies.
170: - **Treating lanes as dogma** — the "Claude coordinates / OpenHands evaluates / Codex implements"
171:   fixed-lane assertion is retired. Lanes are configuration; consult `workflow/lane-policy.md` and
172:   honor the run's recorded lane assignments/overrides in `supervisor.md`/`drift.md`.
173: - **False attached-agent claims** — for Tier-D slices, a Claude `codex:*` skill/helper is not a WSL
174:   Codex daemon thread. Require daemon status plus thread id before claiming the user can see or
175:   steer the subagent from phone/Desktop.
176: - **Carried-in plans as ground truth** — Re-baseline against current `main` before locking the plan.
177: - **Monolithic commits** — Commit by slice, not by monolith. Each slice has its own gate.
178: - **Raw root CLI noise as a verdict** — Package-quality check/lint/fmt evidence must come from the
179:   scoped wrappers, not raw root `deno fmt --check` over Markdown, generated targets, or legacy
180:   line-ending drift (which is not a package-quality verdict source unless the plan explicitly owns
181:   repo-wide formatting). The wrapper invocations and verdict rules live in
182:   `.agents/skills/netscript-tools`.
183: - **Scoped wrappers as a full quality verdict** — the scoped check/lint/fmt wrappers pass code
184:   containing `any` and honor inline `// deno-lint-ignore no-explicit-any`, so a green wrapper run
185:   does NOT prove doctrine/jsr compliance. For any slice touching `packages/**` or `plugins/**`, the
186:   Tier-A slice review MUST additionally run `deno task quality:scan` (fails on `any`+casting and
187:   host-side hardcoded plugin names — the two classes that reached `main` in #745) and
188:   `deno task arch:check` (doctrine fitness), plus the jsr-audit skill for package/plugin waves. A
189:   new `// deno-lint-ignore` or `as unknown as` introduced to green a wrapper is a review-blocking
190:   finding, not a pass. Reviewing on wrappers alone is the exact hole that let #745 merge.
191: 
192: ## Run Artifacts
193: 
194: Run artifacts live under `.llm/runs/<run-id>/` and use templates from `.llm/harness/templates/`.
195: 
196: They are intentionally committed cross-agent context, including the identity, worktree-path,
197: receipt, and resumable-state records needed to continue or audit a run. Do not strip, untrack,
198: redact, or block a PR merely because its scoped run directory contains those records. Secrets and
199: tokens are forbidden in run artifacts. Retention is owner-controlled: after a stable release the
200: owner may select run directories for cleanup and may preserve selected runs across milestones; no
201: agent may perform that cleanup pre-release or infer a deletion set without the owner's instruction.
202: 
203: `<run-id>` is the current branch name with `/` replaced by `-`, followed by `--<suffix>`.
204: 
205: | File                | Purpose                                                                                           |
206: | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
207: | `supervisor.md`     | supervisor identity (model, session, host, paths, branch, baseline, lanes) — written at run start |
208: | `research.md`       | deep findings, re-baseline of carried-in plans                                                    |
209: | `plan.md`           | approved scope, archetype, gates, debt implications                                               |
210: | `implement.md`      | generator prompt when needed                                                                      |
211: | `worklog.md`        | implementation evidence and gate results                                                          |
212: | `plan-eval.md`      | PLAN-EVAL verdict (separate session, before implementation)                                       |
213: | `evaluate.md`       | IMPL-EVAL verdict (separate session, after implementation)                                        |
214: | `context-pack.md`   | resumable summary                                                                                 |
215: | `drift.md`          | append-only drift log                                                                             |
216: | `phase-registry.md` | supervisor runs only: phase-group map + live status                                               |
217: 
218: There is no `commits.md` — the draft-PR commit list + per-slice PR comments are the commit trail.
219: Keep `worklog.md` + `context-pack.md` current as part of every slice. Supervisor runs additionally
220: keep `phase-registry.md`, `final-pr-handoff.md`, and an `escalations/` folder; brief each group
221: agent with `templates/agent-briefing.md`.
222: 
223: Milestone clusters additionally keep `milestone-intake.json`, `milestone-inventory.json`,
224: `milestone-dependency-dag.json`, `milestone-cluster-state.json`, generated `milestone-status.md`,
225: `cut-trace.md`, and `receipts/`. Run `harness:milestone:render` after every state transition and
226: `harness:milestone:validate` before dispatch or release-captain activation. New milestone clusters
227: use schema-v2 `reporting` and the hourly/event-driven owner-facing contract in
228: `workflow/milestone-reporting.md`; its generated report is also the pace/intervention surface.
229: 
230: ## `.llm/runs` Path Caveat
231: 
232: Some search/index tools may skip or lag on freshly written `.llm/runs/` run dirs (the same caveat
233: that applied to the old `.llm/tmp/run/` location). Verify run paths with a direct filesystem listing
234: when needed:
235: 
236: ```powershell
237: dir /s /b ".llm\runs\<id>" 2>&1
238: ```
239: 
240: ## Resource Aggregation
241: 
242: When external docs or examples matter:
243: 
244: 1. check `.resources/deps-docs/`,
245: 2. check `.llm/tmp/docs/`,
246: 3. fetch official/primary docs with available docs tooling,
247: 4. save useful extracts to `.llm/tmp/docs/<source>-<topic>.md`,
248: 5. cite the extract in the run artifact.
249: 
250: ## Evaluator Separation
251: 
252: There are **two** separate-session evaluator phases. Both use the workload tier's typed route from
253: `workflow/lane-policy.md`, and both must differ from the generator by session and vendor family.
254: Provider fallback is capability- and allowance-aware; no lane may self-certify.
255: 
256: **PLAN-EVAL** (before implementation):
257: 
258: - Runs only for genuinely complex or decision-heavy work; quick fixes record `PLAN-EVAL: N/A`.
259: - Runs in a separate session on the evaluator lane selected from `workflow/lane-policy.md`.
260: - Reads `evaluator/plan-protocol.md` + `gates/plan-gate.md`.
261: - Reads `research.md`, `plan.md`, and the `## Design` section.
262: - Writes `plan-eval.md`.
263: - Emits `PASS` or `FAIL_PLAN`.
264: - Follow the selected tier's PLAN-EVAL repair and escalation policy.
265: 
266: **IMPL-EVAL** (final pass, after implementation):
267: 
268: - Runs in a separate session on the evaluator lane selected from `workflow/lane-policy.md`.
269: - Generator writes `worklog.md`, `context-pack.md`, and `drift.md`.
270: - Evaluator reads `.llm/harness/evaluator/protocol.md`, the plan, worklog, context pack, drift, the
271:   draft-PR commit list + per-slice PR comments (the commit trail), selected archetype, overlays, and
272:   gate docs.
273: - Evaluator writes `evaluate.md` with `PASS`, `FAIL_FIX`, `FAIL_RESCOPE`, or `FAIL_DEBT`.
274: - Re-steer the same evaluator and follow the selected tier's IMPL-EVAL maximum and
275:   owner-notification point. Documentation is capped at two rounds.
276: 
277: ## Commit Trail
278: 
279: When a run requires commits, the draft PR's commit list + per-slice PR comments **are** the commit
280: trail — there is no `commits.md`. Per slice:
281: 
282: 1. commit by implementation slice (message names what the slice proves, not what it contains),
283: 2. push the branch,
284: 3. comment on the draft PR with slice scope, commit hash, and gate/test evidence,
285: 4. update `worklog.md` + `context-pack.md` as part of the same slice (a slice whose commit does not
286:    touch the run dir is incomplete),
287: 5. continue to the next slice.
288: 
289: The draft PR is opened in the same session as the first commit, so its commit list is live and
290: reviewable from mobile without cloning or diffing.
291: 
292: ## Rescoping
293: 
294: Rescope when the real work is materially larger than the approved plan or when the selected
295: archetype is wrong. Confirm with the user before expanding scope.
296: 
297: Record rescope evidence in `drift.md` with severity `significant` or `architectural`.
298: 
299: ## Where Lessons Belong
300: 
301: | Content type                                  | Destination                          |
302: | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
303: | Generic run mechanics                         | `.llm/harness/workflow/`             |
304: | Archetype-specific gates or false-done states | `.llm/harness/archetypes/`           |
305: | Stable repeated cross-run lessons             | `.llm/harness/lessons/`              |
306: | Package/plugin doctrine navigation            | `.agents/skills/netscript-doctrine/` |
307: | Deep domain expertise                         | a focused skill                      |
308: | Deferred doctrine violations                  | `.llm/harness/debt/arch-debt.md`     |
309:

315:   -> resuming? read context-pack.md

385: 
386: # NetScript Tools
387: 
388: Use this skill when choosing commands or recording validation evidence in the NetScript repo. The
389: goal is to avoid false green gates, stale git reads, and stale automation comments.
390: 
391: ## Tool Locations
392: 
393: Use `.llm/tools/` for harness, evaluator, agent, and package-quality helper scripts. Fitness gates
394: live under `.llm/tools/fitness/`; keep new doctrine, standards, JSR, and release-readiness helpers
395: there unless they are product-facing CLI features.
396: 
397: Use `tools/` only for reusable product/repository tooling that should ship as part of the public
398: developer surface. Do not create a parallel fitness tree outside `.llm/tools/`.
399: 
400: ## Git And Status
401: 
402: RTK can cache read-heavy git output. For ground-truth branch state, spawn git directly:
403: 
404: ```powershell
405: deno eval 'const p = new Deno.Command("git", { args: ["status", "--short"] }).outputSync(); await Deno.stdout.write(p.stdout); await Deno.stderr.write(p.stderr); Deno.exit(p.code);'
406: deno eval 'const p = new Deno.Command("git", { args: ["ls-remote", "origin", "refs/heads/<branch>"] }).outputSync(); await Deno.stdout.write(p.stdout); await Deno.stderr.write(p.stderr); Deno.exit(p.code);'
407: ```
408: 
409: Use `rtk` for exploratory read-heavy commands when token reduction matters. Do not use filtered RTK
410: output as the sole PASS/FAIL source for gates.
411: 
412: ## Validation Wrappers
413: 
414: ### Durable gate receipts
415: 
416: For CI or long-lived harness workers, invoke allowlisted gates through
417: `.llm/tools/gates/run-gate.ts`; do not redirect an ad-hoc command and call the log a receipt. The
418: runner records the exact argv/cwd, immutable Git head, request hash, attempt, timing, real
419: exit/signal, and bounded hashed output, then atomically replaces one JSON receipt. Same
420: invocation-ID/same-hash calls share one lifecycle-local promise; ID reuse with another hash and
421: capacity exhaustion fail closed. This is at-most-once only within the live broker lifecycle, not a
422: distributed or crash-safe execution lock.
423: 
424: The runner resolves the repository's actual `HEAD` itself. A caller-supplied `--git-head` must
425: match; `--allow-git-head-mismatch <reason>` exists only for explicit diagnostic fixtures and records
426: both values. Such a receipt cannot satisfy an evidence set. Receipts attest that one process ran in
427: one working tree at the recorded commit; they do not attest remote branch currency, source-tree
428: cleanliness, semantic gate sufficiency, or publication. Those remain separate gates.
429: 
430: `PASS` certifies only the named command. Sufficiency is recomputed from exact receipts; never trust
431: or hand-edit a `sufficiency` string. Duplicate gate IDs, duplicate receipt IDs, contradictory
432: receipts, `SKIPPED`, `NOT_RUN`, missing/nonterminal receipts, or an immutable-head mismatch are
433: insufficient. Package/plugin evidence also needs `quality-gate`, dependency evidence, and the
434: applicable JSR audit. E2E tools keep their domain JSON reports; reference them with `--child-report`
435: instead of double-wrapping or replacing them. A declared child report is part of the verdict: it
436: must be freshly written, parse as JSON, and is hashed into the receipt. Missing, malformed, or stale
437: child reports fail closed.
438: 
439: **MANDATE (harness runs).** TS type-check / test / lint / format gate **evidence MUST come from the
440: structured wrappers** — `.llm/tools/run-deno-check.ts`, `.llm/tools/run-deno-test.ts`,
441: `.llm/tools/run-deno-lint.ts`, and `.llm/tools/run-deno-fmt.ts` (invoked directly, or through the
442: `deno task check|test|lint|fmt:check` aliases that already wrap them). Raw root `deno check .` /
443: `deno fmt --check` / `deno lint` over the repo is **not a verdict source**: it walks Markdown,
444: generated output, scratch workspaces, and future-wave packages, producing false reds/greens. Use
445: these wrappers for package/plugin quality checks:
446: 
447: ```powershell
448: deno task check
449: deno task test
450: deno task lint
451: deno task fmt:check
452: deno run --allow-read --allow-run .llm/tools/run-deno-check.ts --root <path> --ext ts,tsx
453: deno run --allow-read --allow-write --allow-run .llm/tools/run-deno-test.ts -- --allow-all <test-path>
454: deno run --allow-read --allow-run .llm/tools/run-deno-lint.ts --root <path> --ext ts,tsx
455: deno run --allow-read --allow-run .llm/tools/run-deno-fmt.ts --root <path> --ext ts,tsx
456: ```
457: 
458: The source wrappers accept roots, extensions, include/exclude filters, and batching; the test
459: wrapper accepts native test arguments after `--`. All emit structured compact output.
460: Package-quality formatting gates target source TypeScript only (`--ext ts,tsx`) and exclude
461: generated output, scratch workspaces, and future-wave packages. All scoped wrappers fail closed when
462: their own selection is empty. Check/test/lint/fmt child crashes must appear structurally in JSON,
463: test failures are grouped without losing affected test locations, and doc-lint preserves its child
464: exit code; an empty findings array is not a PASS when a child failed.
465: 
466: **Code-quality gate (required for `packages/**`/`plugins/**` waves).** The scoped check/lint/fmt
467: wrappers above are necessary but NOT sufficient: they pass code containing `any`, honor an inline
468: `// deno-lint-ignore no-explicit-any`, and do not flag host-side hardcoded plugin-name coupling —
469: the two doctrine violations that reached `main` in the beta.9 CLI wave (#745). Run
470: `deno task
471: quality:gate` (which chains `deno task quality:scan` + `deno task arch:check`) on any
472: framework-wave slice; `deno task quality:scan:repo` audits the whole `packages/cli/src`+`plugins`
473: surface. The scanner (`.llm/tools/quality/scan-code-quality.ts`) fails on
474: `any`/`as unknown as`/`as any`, blanket `no-explicit-any` ignores, and host-side plugin-name checks;
475: the only suppression is an inline `// quality-allow: <reason>` on the offending line (reason
476: required, count reported, `--max-allow <n>` bounds it). CI mirrors this in `code-quality.yml`. A
477: green scoped wrapper is never a substitute for `quality:gate` on framework source.
478: 
479: ## Dependency Evidence
480: 
481: **MANDATE (harness runs).** Any "is this the latest / is this outdated / is this import dead / does
482: the published surface install / any advisories" question MUST be answered through the
483: `.llm/tools/deps/*` wrappers, exposed as `deno task deps:latest|outdated|why|audit|prod-install` —
484: never a hand-rolled registry `curl`, and never `deno outdated --latest` for "latest" (it ignores
485: semver and surfaces pre-release tags as latest). The canonical command map, the
486: `deno outdated
487: --latest` trap rationale, and the `catalog:` npm-only law live once in the
488: **netscript-deno-toolchain** skill — read it there; this skill does not restate those gotchas.
489: 
490: For targeted `deno check` commands that touch workspace code, include `--unstable-kv`:
491: 
492: ```powershell
493: deno check --unstable-kv packages/<pkg>/mod.ts
494: ```
495: 
496: Do not run mutating root `deno task fmt` unless the user explicitly asks for repo-wide formatting
497: changes. Use scoped formatting for owned files only.
498: 
499: ## Publish And Docs
500: 
501: Release automation keeps volatile JSR management endpoints in
502: `.llm/tools/release/config/endpoints.ts`; the non-agentic suite maintenance map is in
503: `.llm/tools/README.md`. Change the config value, not individual release feature modules.
504: 
505: Package publishability gates commonly use:
506: 
507: ```powershell
508: deno doc --lint packages/<pkg>/mod.ts
509: deno task doc:lint --root packages/<pkg> --pretty
510: deno publish --dry-run --allow-dirty
511: deno run --allow-read --allow-run --allow-env .llm/tools/fitness/audit-jsr-package.ts --root packages/<pkg> --text
512: ```
513: 
514: `deno task doc:lint` wraps `.llm/tools/run-deno-doc-lint.ts` — the structured runner for the
515: `deno doc --lint` publish bar. Prefer it when the raw `deno doc --lint` output is too noisy to

517: **full export map**, not `mod.ts` alone, or sibling re-exports false-flag) and emits grouped JSON

519: 
520: Run `deno publish --dry-run --allow-dirty` from the package directory unless the checked-in task or
521: plan says otherwise. Treat raw dry-run output as authoritative for slow types; helper scripts may
522: overcount banner text.

524: ## OpenHands And PR Comments
525: 
526: The `gh` CLI is not reliably available. Use GitHub MCP tools for PR comments. For OpenHands, comment
527: on the PR with the exact trigger text needed for the run. The persistent
528: `<!-- openhands-agent-summary -->` comment can be stale; trust committed artifacts like
529: `plan-eval.md`, `evaluate.md`, and run logs over the summary comment.
530: 
531: When posting automation requests, specify:
532: 
533: - exact one-pass command
534: - repository root as working directory
535: - raw exit code requirement
536: - lock hygiene: do not commit `deno.lock` or source churn unless a reviewed fix requires it

538: ## Supervisor Automation (agentic tools)
539: 
540: ### Resource-hygiene symptoms
541: 
542: If a run failed and you do not know what is still running, `behavior.service-health` timed out,
543: ports are already in use, or a `postgres-*` container exists that you did not start, begin with the
544: read-only `deno task maint:leak-check -- --slice-dir <run-dir> --worktree <worktree>`. It reports
545: owned, foreign, and unknown-owner resources. `deno task maint:teardown -- ...` is dry-run by
546: default; `--apply` is explicit and can act only on positively proven run-owned resources.
547: 
548: Use `deno task maint:dogfood-skills` to install the local CLI's current consumer bundle into
549: `.agents/generated/consumer-skills/`; never fork that bundle by hand.
550: 
551: The supervisor drives Tier-D Codex and Tier-E OpenHands through `.llm/tools/agentic/*`, each exposed
552: as an `agentic:*` `deno task` (see `deno.json` and the index in `.llm/harness/workflow/tooling.md`).
553: Two are durable GitHub infra utilities worth calling out:
554: 
555: - **`gh-watch.ts`** (`deno task agentic:gh-watch --pr <n>`) — token-free CI/verdict watch. Run it as
556:   a **background** process: it polls a PR's OpenHands IMPL/PLAN-EVAL summary comment (and, with
557:   `--run-id`, the triggered Actions run) until the state is terminal, then exits — re-waking the
558:   supervisor turn without a polling loop kept in context. Exit codes: `0` PASS · `10` FAIL · `12`
559:   final-no-verdict · `13` action-run-failed · `2` timeout · `4` no-token. Use it whenever you have
560:   dispatched an evaluator and must wait for the verdict.
561: - **`maint/gh-token.ts`** (`deno task maint:gh-token check|store`) — durable GitHub-token
562:   resolver/store. `check` resolves a token from any healthy source (env candidates → `gh auth token`
563:   Windows/WSL → bounded GCM `git credential fill`), validates it against `GET /user`, and reports
564:   only the source + login (never the token). `store` reads ONE PAT from stdin and persists it to
565:   every durable place (Windows GCM + WSL `gh`) so later sessions auto-resolve. Use `check` at the
566:   start of any GitHub session; use `store` once when the supervisor's token is missing/rotated.
567: 
568: The desired-state runtime controller is the default health/repair entry point:
569: `deno task agentic:runtime doctor|status` for inspect-only environment/session snapshots, and
570: `deno task agentic:runtime repair codex-remote --worktree <path> [--dry-run]` for planned,
571: session-safe Codex daemon repair. `deno task agentic:routing-state` reads the persisted
572: quota-fallback routing state.
573: 
574: Read the pinned Harness fleet routing through `deno task agentic:matrix`, never by shell-scraping
575: TypeScript. NetScript's internal launch resolver and paid OpenCode guard read the same pinned
576: Harness matrix. Use `--tier <tier>` for one row, `--plan-evaluator` or `--impl-evaluator` for a
577: direct evaluator lookup, `--role deep-research` for the dedicated research role,
578: `--fallback-of
579: <logical-model>` to list every context-sensitive fallback, and `--json` for
580: structured consumption. The full table includes separate Deep Research default and fallback columns.
581: 
582: Pure UI/UX specialist routing is an explicit `ui_ux` role; incidental UI changes stay on the normal
583: implementation role. Owner overrides require the typed override record and the exact grant in a
584: repo-relative `.llm/runs/**/worklog.md`. Never bypass the launcher directly: the override does not
585: waive separate-session or different-family evaluation.
586: 
587: The rest of the family (`launch-codex-slice`, `codex-resume`, `codex-status`, `codex-watch`,
588: `dispatch-openhands`, `openhands-status`, `gh-pr`) is indexed in `.llm/harness/workflow/tooling.md`.
589: `.llm/tools/agentic/` is the **only** interface for driving Codex — never ad-hoc `wsl.exe`. The
590: suite is concern-grouped (`codex/`, `openhands/`, `github/`, `wsl/`, `claude/`, `runtime/` +
591: `runtime/cli/`, `lib/`); its `README.md` is the canonical map.
592: 
593: **Monthly maintenance:** fleet route model IDs live in pinned Harness; transitional local provider
594: presets live in `.llm/tools/agentic/config/models.ts`, tool versions in `config/versions.ts`,
595: endpoints in `config/endpoints.ts`; workload and coordinator bindings live in pinned Harness, while
596: `runtime/routing-policy.ts` resolves local provider availability. The "Maintenance map" table in the
597: suite README says exactly where to change a model, version, policy, agent, or dep. A guard test
598: (`config/no-hardcoded-volatile_test.ts`) fails the suite if any of these values is hardcoded outside
599: `config/`.
600: 
601: ## Lock Hygiene
602: 
603: Do not delete lock files or caches. Do not run `deno cache --reload` without approval. If automation
604: or validation mutates `deno.lock`, inspect the diff against the true branch base before accepting
605: it. PLAN-EVAL should not commit lock churn.
606: 
607: ## Worktree Sync
608: 
609: If push rejects due to a remote-only evaluator/bot commit, inspect the remote commit before
610: integrating:
611: 
612: ```powershell
613: deno eval 'const p = new Deno.Command("git", { args: ["show", "--stat", "--oneline", "--name-status", "origin/<branch>"] }).outputSync(); await Deno.stdout.write(p.stdout); await Deno.stderr.write(p.stderr); Deno.exit(p.code);'
614: ```
615: 
616: If the remote commit is unrelated and the local commit should sit on top, use a normal rebase onto
617: `origin/<branch>` and push. Do not discard user or bot commits.
618: 
619: ## Common Gotchas
620: 
621: - `deno task check:packages` and `deno task check:plugins` may not exist; inspect root `deno.json`
622:   and use the available wrapper plus focused checks.
623: - Raw root `deno fmt --check` can include generated/scratch/future-wave files. Prefer scoped wrapper
624:   verdicts.
625: - `deno check .` can walk generated caches and deferred package surfaces. Prefer explicit roots and
